### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with brain and eye anomalies), type A9  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.442)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9913351, Reactome:R-HSA-3000171)

**Proposed mechanism:** LAMC3 (HGNC:6473) —DISRUPTS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal mitochondrial morphology (HP:0003201); DAG1 (HGNC:2388) —DISRUPTS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0011344); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital muscular dystrophy (HP:0008964). Loss-of-function mutations in LAMC3 (MONDO:0013583) and DAG1 (muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy type A9) both disrupt the pathway of extracellular matrix organization, leading to a convergence of downstream cellular and developmental phenotypes including abnormal mitochondrial morphology, global developmental delay, and congenital muscular dystrophy.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in LAMC3 and DAG1 are found to independently affect distinct cellular pathways that do not converge on extracellular matrix organization, or if the shared phenotypes can be fully explained by separate molecular mechanisms. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in the coding regions of LAMC3 or DAG1 in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of extracellular matrix organization in these distinct genetic disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets for improving muscle function and neurodevelopmental outcomes.

#### 2. ataxia - intellectual disability - oculomotor apraxia - cerebellar cysts syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.435)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9913351, Reactome:R-HSA-9925563, Reactome:R-HSA-9981148, Reactome:R-HSA-3000157, Reactome:R-HSA-3000171)

**Proposed mechanism:** LAMC3 (HGNC:6476) —DISRUPTS→ Basement membrane assembly and function (GO:0031012); LAMA1 (HGNC:6472) —DISRUPTS→ Basement membrane assembly and function (GO:0031012); Basement membrane assembly and function (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cerebral white matter morphology (HP:0030176); Basement membrane assembly and function (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar hypoplasia (HP:0001304); Basement membrane assembly and function (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Basement membrane assembly and function (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Oculomotor apraxia (HP:0011227). Mutations in LAMC3 and LAMA1 disrupt the assembly and function of basement membranes, leading to a cascade of downstream effects that manifest as the observed phenotypes in both diseases, including abnormal white matter morphology, cerebellar hypoplasia, intellectual disability, and oculomotor apraxia.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in LAMC3 or LAMA1 that are associated with loss-of-function and demonstrate significant overlap in the resulting phenotypes between Disease A and Disease B would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if variants in these genes lead to distinct molecular pathways or completely unrelated phenotypes, or if mutations in other genes are found to be the primary drivers of one of the diseases without affecting basement membrane function, this hypothesis would be weakened. _(variant: Discovery of a common, highly frequent (e.g., >1% allele frequency in relevant populations) pathogenic variant in LAMC3 or LAMA1 within gnomAD that is linked to either disease would falsify the causal role of rare variants in these genes for these conditions.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of LAMC3 and LAMA1 in basement membrane integrity could pave the way for identifying common therapeutic targets or strategies for both diseases, potentially focusing on enhancing basement membrane repair or compensating for its dysfunction.

Loss-of-function mutations in LAMC3 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to congenital muscular dystrophy. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in DAG1 also disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The shared disruption of extracellular matrix organization represents the mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in DAG1 in patients diagnosed with MONDO:0013583, or absence of mutations in LAMC3 in patients diagnosed with MONDO:0013440. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying shared pathways in muscular dystrophies can inform therapeutic strategies targeting extracellular matrix integrity or muscle repair mechanisms, potentially benefiting patients with either disease.

#### 4. Duchenne muscular dystrophy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.414)

Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in DMD disrupt the dystrophin-associated glycoprotein complex, causing muscle weakness and scoliosis. Both diseases converge on the broad concept of disrupted structural integrity within cellular and extracellular components, with MONDO:0013583 affecting extracellular matrix and DMD affecting the muscle cell membrane complex.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that mutations in LAMC3 and DMD do not lead to loss-of-function phenotypes in MONDO:0013583 and Duchenne muscular dystrophy, respectively, or if the identified mutations are common benign variants in gnomAD. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic variants in LAMC3 and DMD from gnomAD populations at high frequency.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic theme of structural integrity disruption, despite distinct genes, may reveal common therapeutic targets or strategies for diseases affecting connective tissues and muscle, such as those aimed at stabilizing cellular structures or supporting extracellular matrix components.

#### 8. Becker muscular dystrophy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.314)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9913351, Reactome:R-HSA-3000171)

**Proposed mechanism:** Disease-specific variant in LAMC3 —DISRUPTS→ LAMC3 (HGNC:29600); LAMC3 (HGNC:29600) —LEADS_TO→ Basement membrane assembly and integrity; Basement membrane assembly and integrity —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Disease-specific variant in DMD —DISRUPTS→ DMD (HGNC:2924); DMD (HGNC:2924) —LEADS_TO→ Dystrophin-glycoprotein complex function; Dystrophin-glycoprotein complex function —LEADS_TO→ Progressive muscle weakness (HP:0003690); Basement membrane assembly and integrity —BINDS→ Dystrophin-glycoprotein complex function. Variants in LAMC3 lead to defects in basement membrane assembly and integrity, impacting neuronal development and causing intellectual disability. Variants in DMD disrupt the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex, impairing sarcolemmal stability and leading to progressive muscle weakness. The proposed overlap is that proper basement membrane assembly (n2) is intrinsically linked to the function of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex (n6), suggesting a shared downstream cellular machinery.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in LAMC3 do not affect the expression or function of components of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex, or that mutations in DMD do not impact basement membrane composition or integrity, would falsify this hypothesis. Specifically, if targeted molecular assays show no interaction or dependency between LAMC3-dependent basement membrane structures and the dystrophin complex in relevant cell types.

**Why it matters:** Understanding this mechanistic link could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both cognitive and muscular manifestations. For instance, therapies aimed at stabilizing the extracellular matrix or enhancing sarcolemmal repair mechanisms might offer benefit in both conditions, despite their different primary genetic causes.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared impact on cellular integrity, even if initiated by different genes, could reveal common therapeutic targets for preserving muscle function in both genetic cardiomyopathies and other muscular dystrophies.
